channel.title: MCP Monitor Daily Report
channel.description: Daily monitoring of Model Context Protocol mentions

item.title: GitHub - lifan-builds/faster-mac-use: Background-first, multi-cursor browser and native macOS computer-use engine for AI agents · GitHub
item.description: Teaching your AI agent to click around your Mac without stealing your mouse, now with an MCP server that actually keeps its hands off your focus.

item.title: Alasco Assistant Shares Tools With MCP Server | Dirty Static
item.description: Alasco got tired of keeping two copies of the same tools in sync, so its finance chat and its MCP server now share one registry. The chat also keeps working after you close the tab.

item.title: How I gave Claude, Cursor and Codex one shared memory in plain Markdown - DEV Community
item.description: Tired of re-explaining your projects to every AI app you open? One student decided the memory should live in a folder on their own disk, and the apps can all borrow it through MCP.

item.title: GitHub - mozilla/firefox-mcp: Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets AI agents browse the web and debug web pages with Firefox · GitHub
item.description: Firefox learns to take orders from a language model, with a sensible warning label on the bottle: point it at a throwaway profile, not your bank.

item.title: PulsePost by Nindzia: social media scheduler
item.description: Your social media calendar now answers to robots too. PulsePost lets AI assistants plan your posts, provided you remember to click Authorize.

item.title: Flashbox: a pay-per-command sandbox for AI agents
item.description: Turns out waiting is free and rm -rf has an undo button. Your agent's sandbox, priced by the command rather than by the hour.

item.title: GitHub - graphvein/graphvein: From any route, call, handler or table to what it connects to, across your frontends, backends and database. Local, labelled, no LLM. · GitHub
item.description: A code map that traces every route to its callers and tables without asking a language model for help, and then hands that map to coding agents through a read-only MCP server.

item.title: Connect Dealectics to your assistant: Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, Mistral, Perplexity
item.description: One pasted address, a few clicks, and your chatbot becomes a bargain hunter. No account, no API key, just a server URL and a lot of copy-paste.

item.title: GitHub - doors-dev/neui · GitHub
item.description: A Go web framework that hands your app an AI agent with its own workbench, plus MCP connectors, so the agent can finally do more than just chat about your buttons.

item.title: Human feedback, as an API · Voom
item.description: Your coding agent can now recruit a stranger to poke at your app and report back, which is either a breakthrough in quality assurance or the first time your robot has had to ask for a favor.

item.title: What is MCP in LLM/AI? - IT Consulting & IT Training
item.description: Think of an MCP server as a toolbox for language models: the client walks up, asks what's inside, and grabs the calculator without anyone having to explain what a calculator is.

item.title: Google gives AI agents 69 days to move to Workspace MCP · Vortner
item.description: Google decided agents must speak MCP to reach your Workspace data, and the one path the company insists on is also the one that starts charging from the first request. Sixty-nine days to read the fine

item.title: Google Workspace: MCP-Server für KI-Agenten jetzt für alle verfügbar - All About Security Das Online-Magazin zu Cybersecurity (Cybersicherheit). Ransomware, Phishing, IT-Sicherheit, Netzwerksicherheit, KI, Threats, DDoS, Identity & Access, Plattformsicherheit
item.description: Google hands AI agents the keys to your inbox and calendar, but promises six guardrails and a daily quota of 5,000 calls per product to keep things tidy.

item.title: GitHub - Breaktroughf1/lockward: Lockward pins every skill, MCP server, hook and rules file your AI coding agents load, then blocks anything that changes without approval. It works offline across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Gemini CLI, and outputs SARIF and CycloneDX AI-BOMs. Think of it as a lockfile plus a CI policy gate for agent supply chains. · GitHub
item.description: A lockfile for your AI agent's toolbox: it notices when an MCP server or skill quietly changes overnight and refuses to let it slide through CI.

item.title: Google Workspace cambia el acceso de agentes a Gmail y Drive | Nelbytes
item.description: Google decided AI agents should knock on the front door from now on: MCP servers, audit logs, and a billing meter that starts ticking in April.

item.title: Gmail MCP Prompts Don’t Stop Shell-Access Agents - Suncly
item.description: Google's MCP confirmation prompts were meant to keep a human in the loop, but it turns out a cron job and a determined coding agent can click 'allow' just fine.

item.title: Best Crypto and blockchain MCP servers (November 2026) · tested every night
item.description: A leaderboard of 478 crypto MCP servers, re-tested every night, with a helpful reminder that some tool definitions eat 175,000 tokens of context.

item.title: Blofeld - Property-based testing for MCP servers
item.description: Fuzzing your MCP server used to mean writing test cases nobody wanted to write. Now you can hand the job to your coding agent and let it find the bugs for you.

item.title: MCP vs Traditional APIs: Why AI Agents Need a New Protocol - Pocket Casts
item.description: Teaching an AI to talk to your database, your payments and your chat app used to mean a small mountain of bespoke code. This episode asks whether one shared protocol could flatten that mountain.

item.title: Which MCP servers work with Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and VS Code · BOTERNITY MCP Index
item.description: Turns out most remote MCP servers will happily plug into Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or VS Code, provided you trust a nightly robot's homework.

item.title: What is an MCP gateway, and when do you need one? | Izylife Solutions
item.description: Your first MCP server takes thirty seconds to set up. The fifth one is when someone asks who ran that command, and nobody can say.

item.title: Google Will Make AI Agents Use Its Workspace MCP Servers. The Gmail One Can't Send Email | Tech Stackups
item.description: Google has decided that if your AI agent wants to touch your inbox, it'll go through Google's MCP gate, and the gate conveniently can't send email. Partners, however, seem to have a key.

item.title: Why you still need a CMS in the AI era
item.description: AI makes the first version of a website cheap. Keeping the menu, prices and opening hours correct across every page is still the expensive part, and that is what a CMS is for.

item.title: GitHub - Tthanh2k6/turbo-desktop: Windows desktop automation MCP server (UIA + WinRT OCR, InputLock safety, EN/VI) and Turbo Remote control hub · GitHub
item.description: Turns out giving an AI agent the keys to your Windows desktop is much less scary when someone builds a deny list, a panic button, and a hash-chained audit log for it.

item.title: BOTERNITY log, 2026-11-25
item.description: Every night someone checks all 33,419 public MCP servers, so you don't have to. Most answer, a good number are broken, and a few have quietly grown 17 tools into 84.

item.title: Suncly launches AI agent reliability index with Cloudflare topping blind-spot list
item.description: Turns out many AI agent servers are about as forthcoming as a tax auditor on a Monday. Suncly's new index checked who tells agents what they can actually do.

item.title: NL-GOV-MCP · Dutch public-sector data in one AI interface
item.description: Dutch bureaucracy finally gets a single front door, and the AI on the other side can actually read the paperwork.

item.title: What is MCP? | Vignesh Rajendran
item.description: Hiring a capable AI assistant is pointless if it sits at an empty desk with no logins. MCP is the shared language that finally hands it the keys, and the second version teaches it some office manners.

item.title: BOTERNITY · Open infrastructure for AI agents
item.description: Infrastructure for agents that want to read the web, audit MCP servers, and remember things between sessions, all without signing up for anything or asking an AI to guess.
